name: Transfer Press
author: Ruman Ahmed

sections.description:
Transfer Press is the simplest way to move plugins from one WordPress site to another. Download any installed plugin as a ready-to-install ZIP, upload it on another site, or connect your sites and push or pull plugins directly from the dashboard. No FTP, file manager or SSH needed.

It is built for people who look after more than one site: developers moving custom plugins from staging to live, agencies setting up client sites with the same toolkit, and site owners who want a safe copy of a plugin before they update it.

Every import is reviewed before anything changes. You see the version, the files and whether the site meets the plugin’s PHP and WordPress requirements. When you replace a plugin, the current version is backed up first and restored automatically if the new one fails. Roll back to any backup in one click.

Version 3.0 brings every former Pro feature into the free plugin: bulk export, backups and restore, transfer history, site-to-site push and pull, schedules, email notifications and WP-CLI. There is no paid version.

What Transfer Press moves

Transfer Press moves plugin files. It does not copy plugin settings stored in the database, posts, pages, users, themes or media. To move a whole site, use a full-site migration tool.

Features

  • Export any plugin as a ZIP, or many at once in one download (runs in the background with progress).
  • Exclusion rules keep node_modules, .git, logs and test files out of exports, with a preview.
  • Safe import: every archive is checked for unsafe paths, blocked file types and PHP/WordPress requirements before anything changes.
  • Replace with confidence: see installed vs uploaded versions and required plugins, confirm, and the old version is backed up first and restored automatically if anything fails.
  • Backups and one-click restore for any plugin.
  • Site-to-site transfer: pull from or push to your other sites using scoped, expiring API keys, with checksum verification.
  • Schedules: export or sync plugins hourly, daily, weekly or monthly.
  • History, logs and diagnostics: who did what and when, plus a system check for support.
  • Email notifications for transfers, backups, schedules and failures.
  • WP-CLI: wp transferpress list | export | import | bulk-export | pull | push | backups | backup | rollback | schedules | sites | run-jobs.

Exports and backups are stored in protected folders and only downloadable through short-lived links. Installing, replacing and restoring require the install_plugins capability.

Source code

The admin screens are built with Vue and Vite, so the plugin ships compiled files in public/build/. The full, human-readable source code (including resources/ and framework/ui/) is on GitHub: https://github.com/RumanCodes/transfer-press

To build it yourself: npm ci && npm run build. The PHP code needs no build step.

License

This plugin is licensed under the GPLv2 or later.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins → Add New, or upload the ZIP.
  2. Activate Transfer Press.
  3. Open Transfer Press in the admin menu.
sections.faq:
How do I download an installed plugin as a ZIP?

Open Transfer Press → Export and click Export next to the plugin. You get a ZIP that installs on any WordPress site through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or through Transfer Press → Import. Select several plugins to download them in one archive.

Can I migrate plugins between two WordPress sites?

Yes. Export and import a ZIP, or install Transfer Press on both sites, connect them under Remote sites with an API key, and pull or push plugins directly.

Does it copy plugin settings or my content?

No. Transfer Press moves the plugin’s files. Settings that a plugin stores in the database, and your posts, pages, users and media, stay where they are.

Can I roll back a plugin to an earlier version?

Yes. Transfer Press backs up a plugin before replacing it, and you can back up any plugin yourself. Restore a backup from Transfer Press → Backups in one click.

What happens if the plugin already exists?

You’re shown both versions and asked to confirm. The current copy is backed up and restored automatically if the new one fails to install.

Can I transfer premium plugins?

Yes. Licensed plugins often tie the license to a domain, so you may need to reactivate the license on the destination site.

Is FTP required?

No, but your host must allow direct writes to the plugins folder. Settings → System shows whether it does.

Is it safe?

Archives are checked for unsafe paths, blocked file types and requirements before anything is installed. Installing, replacing and restoring need the install_plugins capability. Site-to-site transfers use API keys that can be limited to listing, pulling or pushing, can expire, and only do what the user who created them is allowed to do. Downloads are verified with SHA-256 checksums.

What does my server need?

PHP 8.0 or later with the Zip extension, WordPress 5.9 or later, and permission for WordPress to write to the plugins folder. Transfer Press → Settings → System checks all of this for you.

Does it work with WP-CLI?

Yes. Run wp transferpress to list, export, import, back up, roll back, push and pull plugins from the command line. This is the best option for very large plugins.

Does it work on multisite?

It works per site. Network-wide management is not supported yet.

Did Transfer Press Pro come?

All of its features are in this plugin, for free. No Pro version will release!
sections.changelog:
3.0.0 – November 25, 2026

  • New: every former Pro feature is included — bulk export, exclusion rules, backups/restore, history, remote push/pull, API keys, schedules, notifications, WP-CLI.
  • New: automatic backup before replacing a plugin, and automatic restore if installation fails.
  • New: requirement, version and dependency checks before installing; SHA-256 verification on pulls.
  • New: background jobs with progress and cancel; logs; system diagnostics; settings export/import.
  • New: rebuilt admin interface.
  • Security: fixed issues in import confirmation, remote pull and export downloads; stricter capabilities; protected storage; authenticated encryption for stored keys; no third-party fonts.
  • Changed: API keys can only do what the user who created them may do. Keys made before 3.0 can no longer receive pushes; generate a new key on sites that receive pushes. Pull schedules made before 3.0 must be created again.
  • Fix: exporting single-file plugins; large plugins over 5 000 files; scheduled exports being deleted.
  • Changed: requires WordPress 5.9+, PHP 8.0+ with the Zip extension. Developer-facing changes: https://github.com/RumanCodes/transfer-press/blob/main/UPGRADE.md

2.4.5 – August 2, 2026

  • Maintenance release.

2.4.4 – August 2, 2026

  • Updated contributors, donate link, and author URI.

2.4.3 – August 2, 2026

  • Updated author URI.

2.4.2 – July 17, 2026

  • Update changelog

2.4.1 – June 17, 2026

  • Minor bug fixes and improvements.

2.4.0 – June 16, 2026

  • Import now respects the configured maximum upload size instead of a hardcoded 2 MB client-side limit.
  • Upload card now shows the actual allowed upload size.
  • Improved user interface.

2.3.1 – May 30, 2026

  • Raised default plugin import upload size from 2 MB to a consistent 5 MB.
  • Fixed inconsistent upload size defaults.
  • UI/UX improvements.

2.2.1 – March 31, 2026

  • Fixed PHP warning.

2.2.0 – March 30, 2026

  • Enhanced security with proper capability checks and nonce verification.
  • Added file size validation for plugin uploads.
  • Improved error handling throughout the plugin.
  • Fixed version inconsistencies across plugin files.
  • Enhanced input sanitization and output escaping.
  • Fixed code style and formatting issues.

2.0.0 – June 10, 2025

  • Added header.
  • Replaced the old file selection dropdown with Vue 3 Multiselect fields.
  • Added user guide and documentation.
  • Improved the Export page.
  • Improved the Import page.

1.0.0 – April 19, 2025

  • Initial public release.
  • Export and download plugin ZIP files.
  • Upload and import plugin ZIP files.
  • Activate plugins after import.
  • Toast notifications and visual feedback.
